title: RAW UNREVIEWED: production-neighbour spelling drift follows independently reconstructed unfolded-sheet order
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Compare a bounded codicologically justified order in which an unfolded bifolium could have been written with present reading order. Short-lived spelling preferences should predict nonadjacent sheet neighbours if those were consecutive work surfaces. No unrestricted permutation search or assumption that current binding preserves chronology.

design.mechanism: Short-lived copying or pen-session habits persist across consecutive production surfaces, including faces not adjacent in finished reading order.
design.unit: Independently documented complete bifolium with admitted faces and same-hand comparable text; whole-sheet holdout.
design.contrast: A small externally fixed set of unfolded-sheet work orders versus current reading order, same-hand distant controls and same-section ecology.
design.prediction: Transient orthographic residuals predict the next physical work face under the external sheet order on unseen sheets better than the reading-order alternative; no result if order or capacity is unbound.
design.scope: RAW proposal only. IL003 multiscale boundary precedent must be reviewed; this proposes work-order prediction on physical sheets, not another boundary-scale scan. Needs provenance-clean physical collation, admitted faces and sufficient same-hand overlap. No text or images accessed for proposal.
